title: Example 18-9: Diagramming with Underlining

illustrates.quote: Linear diagramming shows sentence structure, using font attributes to distinguish between parts of speech. Use transcriber-defined typeform indicators if needed (as seen for the double underlining in the example below). Use 1-3 margins for each diagrammed sentence.

blocks.text: In the following sentence the single underlined word is the verb and the double underlined words are a prepositional phrase.
We <u>arrived</u> at the hotel in the evening.
blocks.features: 'arrived' single underlined (the verb); 'at the hotel' DOUBLE underlined (prepositional phrase) -- the double underline is not expressible in the builder's markup. Sentence set flush left at the box margin.

print.printFeatures: single underline under 'arrived', double underline under 'at the hotel'

braille.notes: Re-extracted from source (lines 14629-14633, margin 9); matches both runs byte-for-byte.

resolution: Braille already agreed and re-extraction confirms it exactly; the diagrammed sentence and its single/double-underline distinction confirmed by back-translation. Kept the intro sentence as an ordinary, representable paragraph but the diagrammed sentence itself as 'other' (F-188 + F-189 both apply and neither is fixable by choosing different wording). Print description corrected 23 Sep 2026 (see printCorrections).

printCorrections.now: paragraph + a flush paragraph 'We <u>arrived</u> at the hotel in the evening.' (double underline on 'at the hotel' noted in features only)
